fields.title: Logging is mandatory, structured and tiered
fields.decision: Every Mapper entry point and data method takes an `ILogger`; it is not optional. ArgentSea logs through precompiled `LoggerMessage` definitions with fixed, numbered event ids (connection-string built, expression-tree creation, parameter or column not found, mapper cache status, mapper trace, unexpected DbNull, invalid reader, command executed, connect or command retry, circuit breaker, batch step). Each event has a fixed level. Critical: circuit breaker tripped. Error: reader closed or null, with connection context. Warning: retry started. Information: breaker test and recovery. Debug: why a required mapping returned null, rendered generated mapper code, missing parameters, delegate cache misses. Trace: per-property mapping progress and command execution times. Logs always carry the query name and connection description.
fields.context: Data-tier failures in a sharded, concurrent system are hard to diagnose. An exception thrown on one of many worker threads loses context, compiled mapping code cannot be stepped through in a debugger, and retries hidden in a driver make degradation invisible. A supportable application needs logs by design (principle p6: never hide resilience activity).

alternatives.option: An optional logger, with no logging when none is supplied.
alternatives.whyRejected: Diagnostics would silently disappear exactly where they are needed most.
It allocates on every call, even when the level is disabled, and gives no stable event ids to alert on.

fields.consequences: Operators can alert on stable event ids, such as breaker trips and retries, and trace any failure to a query and endpoint. Debug and Trace levels expose the Mapper's generated code and per-property progress for troubleshooting. Debug and Trace are expensive and should not run in production, so the log level is a performance setting. Every call site must have a logger available.
